publications.assertionSummary: Vitals — Marriage(s): 'Grizzell Fletcher — a much-married Braintree widow, married at Braintree on 12 November 1661; John was her fourth husband.'

incoming.explanation: The resolved town-record reading corroborates the (independently attested) second marriage to Grizzell.
Grisel's will, naming her as already wife to John Burge, extends the Fletcher-Jewell-Griggs-Kibby-Gurney-Burge remarriage chain established for Grizzell in the wives-and-marriages unit.

outgoing.explanation: Cross-unit: the Braintree marriage and wife-death lines, now read as Gurney, qualify the record-coverage negative that no vital record fixes John's life events — two Braintree town-record vital lines do survive for him, under a misread surname, though they still fix neither his birth nor his origin.

shortLabel: Second marriage: John Gurney m. widow Grizzell, Braintree 12 Nov 1661

sources.alignmentNote: The Braintree town record's own marriage line (printed under the misread 'Cheny' surname, resolved to Gurney by RI-000061) - the primary-record witness to the marriage alongside the compiled tag-10-70 and torrey.
Holman names the groom 'John Gurney Sr.' directly; establishes the marriage independently of the Braintree town-record surname reading.
sources.excerpt: 12 Nov. 1661 Braintree, by Peter Brackett, John Gurney Sr.

statement: John Gurney married the widow Grizzell — 'Grissell of the many marriages' — at Braintree on 12 November 1661, by Peter Brackett, as the fourth of her five husbands (Thomas Jewell, Humphrey Griggs, Henry Kibby, John Gurney, and, after John's 1663 death, John Burge in 1667). The marriage is attested directly as John Gurney by Holman's TAG marriage-chain study and by Torrey, independent of the misread town record. Grizzell's compiled maiden name Fletcher (daughter of Robert Fletcher of Chelmsford, Essex) is a colonial attribution and carries no bearing on John Gurney's English origin.
